name: Sequencer
description: Record, loop and erase scenes on the pads
changelog: 0.12.0: EDIT on a kit track's seq view opens the Sampler on that track's kit -- no more "Kit 2 plays as it is" -- once the kits' engine holds it (a toast while it loads). Requires core 2.42.
0.10.1: a track whose scene the sequencer lacks gets the scene just added, not the active one (core 2.7, AudioSong::sceneForNewSeq). Requires core 2.7.

0.10.0: opened from MODE, the screen is the song's armed kit track (Arrange's ARM), of up to two; the seq view of a second kit track's block plays that track's kit, and EDIT there says the kit is changed from the track's menu in Arrange instead of opening the Sampler on the other one. Requires core 2.2.

0.9.1: builds on core 1.70+/gui 1.28+ and on core/gui 2.x (>=1.70.0,<3.0.0 and >=1.28.0,<3.0.0) for the merge window; a root deleted before the app's teardown is handled (gui 2.0 calls destroy with none)

0.9.0: opened from an Arrange track (CLIP EDIT on a seq block, or from MODE on a song with a kit seq track) this screen is one block of it -- the one picked, or the one under Arrange's playhead -- named T<track> B<bar>: its notes are put in the track's scene and looped here on their own, and what is recorded, erased, doubled or cleared goes back to the block as it changes, a block as long as its notes following x2 and /2. On a bar with no block the first notes made become one. Recording against the arrangement is Arrange's REC now, so PLAY here no longer runs the song, and the scene keys do not step away from the block. A block longer than a scene holds (8 bars, 192 notes) is left to Arrange, with a note saying so. Requires core 1.58 (ISongEngine::openSeqEdit).

0.8.1: opened from MODE on a song with a seq track that plays the kit, the screen is that track, as Arrange's EDIT opens it -- REC goes into the scene the track plays and PLAY runs with the song. It recorded into whatever scene was up, and Arrange showed the track empty and silent. A song without such a track keeps the groove sequencer.

0.8.0: one screen, from MODE or from an Arrange track -- the same soft keys either way: ARR, EDIT (the Sampler or Pitch Play, whichever the notes play through), x2, /2, BOUNCE, ERASE and a new CLEAR that takes every note of the scene on show (pressed twice). The click is the transport bar's key; the count-in moved to the scene window (PRE).

0.7.0: 16 LEVELS in the scene window -- the Sampler's own mode (off, velocity, pitch), with the pad it plays, so a part of one pad at sixteen loudnesses or sixteen semitones is recorded here. Each hit keeps what it sounded as, so the part plays the same with the mode off again. Usable while SRC is the kit. Needs core 1.55 (PadPerformance).

0.6.0: the instrument source plays exactly what Pitch Play is set to -- its key, scale, transpose and chord, read from core InstrumentPlayState instead of a chromatic map and a chord index of our own. The Pads and Chord -/+ rows are gone; one read-only line says what Pitch Play has. Needs core 1.49.

0.5.0: a Chord row in the SRC window -- a pad plays a chord, not one note, through MusicTheory's types and progressions; the held notes are kept per pad so a release lets go of all of them. Needs core 1.44 (the ninths and the progression table).

0.4.0: SRC on the transport row picks what the pads record -- the loaded kit, or an instrument from Pitch Play's library, borrowed through IInstrumentHost and given back when the source goes back to KIT or the screen closes. The pads then play it chromatically from a base note the window sets (16 pads = 16 semitones). A bounce captures the pads bus, so it records whichever is playing; requires core 1.38 for the instrument host.
0.3.2: BPM: a value being turned reads dark on the accent: the text colour sits on the button, which is the only thing ever EDITED, not on its label
0.3.1: builds on the PC against LVGL 9.4 (0.2.1 merged in)

0.3.0: SYNC on the transport (the song's switch): PLAY, REC and DUB from a stop start the arrangement and the sequencer with it, STOP stops both; pad 1 at the bottom of the grid; tempo is a button that shows the whole number, clicked to turn and clicked to leave (a spinbox scrolled its digits out of sight); requires core 1.23 and gui 1.13
0.2.0: tempo field follows a host's MIDI clock and refuses edits while it drives (from the Sampler, ae3dc82); count-in is one bar of the metre; requires core 1.21 and gui 1.12
